short: A British-Indian garrison was forced to surrender to Ottoman forces in Mesopotamia after a prolonged siege.
full:
On 7 December 1915, a British-Indian army under Major General Charles Townshend retreated to the town of Kut-al-Amara on the Tigris river after a failed advance on Baghdad. They were swiftly surrounded by Ottoman forces commanded by Halil Pasha and the German general Colmar von der Goltz. Despite multiple costly relief attempts by British forces downriver, the garrison remained trapped and slowly starved.

On 29 April 1916, after 147 days of siege, Townshend surrendered unconditionally. Over 13,000 British and Indian troops were taken prisoner, many of whom subsequently died in brutal captivity. The surrender was a severe blow to British prestige in the Middle East, prompting a complete reorganization of their Mesopotamian campaign before Baghdad was finally captured the following year.
